misconceptions.believed: That test_the_starter_answers_wrongly_rather_than_crashing, written one session earlier, documented a premise. It asserted assertIn('return []', starter).
misconceptions.revealed_by: It failed the moment the starter changed, which was the very next session and for a reason the user asked for.
misconceptions.corrected_to: The premise the test exists to protect is that the starter runs and is wrong, because that is what makes it exercise the wrong-answer repair path rather than the crash path. It now asserts exactly that via _check, and is immune to the next redesign of the level's text.
misconceptions.generalisable_lesson: A test pinned to an implementation detail passes happily while the thing it was meant to protect rots, and only complains when something unrelated changes. This one failed loudly and immediately, which is the lucky version. Set against M37: this session the accuracy figures were measured before being written down, not guessed.

decisions.decision: A boss starter runs real work and gets one thing wrong
decisions.rationale: The fight's whole pitch is watching code execute, and a stub gives one line of trace. A correct starter would break the contract that a starter must not pass its own step.

decisions.decision: Each bug is chosen to be visible in the trace
alternatives: Any wrong answer would satisfy the tests
decisions.rationale: A bug you can only see in the verdict is a bug the debugger did not help you find, which wastes the feature the fight exists to show off.
The heal scales with 1 - accuracy. A starter that passes nothing hands over the maximum heal every time and W6's curve never does its job.

decisions.decision: 'Runs', 'watchable' and 'not hopeless' are enforced tests, not prose
decisions.rationale: M36's cost was an invariant nothing tested drifting for two trajectories. Q75 asks which rules can be given a test; these three can, so they were.

friction.description: Designing a bug that fails partially is harder than designing one that fails. Two candidates for summarise were discarded: forgetting the round passed almost everything and made the starter's difficulty depend on float error and therefore on the seed, and dropping the filter failed everything. Ignoring quantity fails four of six cases for a reason a player can name.

handoff.state: Q79's first half is answered and shipped. All three starters run, each fails visibly in the trace, and they pass 50%, 83% and 33% so the repairs cost 5, 2 and 7. Three new contract tests keep it that way. A full play-through lands the boss on 65 rather than 73. 988 tests green unpinned, 964 pinned, verify clean on 45 reference runs.
handoff.next_action: The user plays it. Twice now the useful findings have come from running the game rather than the suite, and the suite has never been the thing that was wrong. Q80 is the open half of Q79 and needs deciding before W7, because scoring a fight whose best outcome is unreachable would bake the problem in. Then T3 W7, boss scoring at 40/30/30, still the only waypoint between T3 and its exit criteria.

open_questions.question: BOSS DOWN is still unreachable from the starters, because the contract says a starter must fail its own tests and every failure costs a repair.
